- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early to avoid overcorrection.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if recent 18-day average is below 70.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.20), model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in first 3–5 periods.  
- When true outcome deviates >10% from 18-day moving average, model is biased — apply mean reversion correction: forecast = 18-day MA + 0.5×(true - MA) for next 3 periods.
